title: lean Ethereum
quote: Lean consensus is beacon chain 2.0: hardened for ultimate security and decentralization, plus finality in seconds; lean data is blobs 2.0: post-quantum blobs, plus granular blob sizing for a calldata-like developer experience; lean execution is EVM 2.0: a minimal, SNARK-friendly instruction set (possibly RISC-V), boosting performance. Motivating trends: the explosive rise of SNARKs and the looming quantum threat, to which hash-based cryptography offers a compelling, unified answer. Targets: 1 gigagas/sec on L1 (10K TPS), 1 teragas/sec on L2. Design philosophy: Minimalism. Modularity. Encapsulated complexity. Formal verification. Provable security.

title: Lean Consensus Roadmap
quote: Four pillars: Lean Consensus (redesigned consensus with rapid finality), Lean Cryptography (hash-based signatures compatible with SNARKs and quantum resistance), Lean Governance (bundling protocol upgrades), Lean Craft (minimalism, modularity, formal verification). Tracks: 3-Slot Finality (3SF) reduces finality from ~15 minutes to seconds; Attester-Proposer Separation; exit queue improvements; hash-based multi-signatures (XMSS-based alternatives to BLS); signature aggregation via zkVM; Poseidon cryptanalysis; formal verification of FRI, STIR, WHIR in Lean 4. Devnets: pq-devnet-0 (Oct 2025), pq-devnet-1 (Dec 2025), pq-devnet-2 (Jan 2026, leanMultisig aggregation), pq-devnet-3 (Feb 2026, separated aggregator role), pq-devnet-4 (target Mar 2026, recursive aggregation via leanVm), pq-devnet-5 (planned, block-level aggregation proof and Goldfish fork choice).

title: pq.ethereum.org — Post-Quantum Ethereum
quote: Quantum computers running Shor's algorithm could recover private keys from public keys, enabling forged signatures. Most engineering roadmaps place cryptographic relevance in the early-to-mid 2030s. The expected L1 protocol upgrade completion is targeted for 2029. leanXMSS is the hash-based signature scheme replacing BLS for validator authentication; leanSig is its Rust implementation; leanVM is a minimal zkVM for aggregation; leanSpec is an executable Python specification used by ~10 client teams. Because post-quantum signatures are larger and lack BLS's native aggregation properties, a SNARK-based aggregation approach using a minimal zkVM (leanVM) is being developed to restore scalability. The approach prioritizes cryptographic agility — the ability to upgrade core primitives without destabilizing the network.

title: 3-Slot-Finality Protocol for Ethereum
quote: Gasper, the consensus protocol currently employed by Ethereum, typically requires 64 to 95 slots -- the units of time during which a new chain extending the previous one by one block is proposed and voted -- to finalize. ... To address these issues and speed up finality, we introduce a partially synchronous finality gadget, which we combine with two dynamically available consensus protocols ... This integration results in secure ebb-and-flow protocols [SP 2021], achieving finality within three slots after a proposal and realizing 3-slot finality.

title: leanEthereum/leanSpec — Ethereum protocol specifications and test vector generation
quote: Formal specifications written in Python 3.12+ with Pydantic models for type safety. Specifies protocol definitions and fork logic, cryptographic subspecifications (Poseidon, KoalaBear, XMSS), SSZ serialization, observability and networking, state transition and fork choice rules. Actively maintained with 1,048 commits; 143 stars, 80 forks.

title: leanEthereum/leanSig — synchronized signatures based on tweakable hash functions and incomparable encodings
quote: A prototypical Rust library for synchronized signatures based on tweakable hash functions and incomparable encodings, designed for research and benchmarking rather than production use. Generalized XMSS scheme; hardcoded instantiations using Poseidon. The code has not been audited and is not meant to be used in production.

title: Hash-Based Multi-Signatures for Post-Quantum Ethereum
venue: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive / IACR Communications in Cryptology
quote: Introduces a family of hash-based signature schemes as post-quantum alternatives to BLS for Ethereum proof-of-stake, where validators independently sign blocks and signatures are publicly aggregated into a compact aggregate signature. The proposed schemes are variants of the XMSS signature scheme, analyzed within a unified framework designed to minimize security loss and facilitate efficient parameter selection. A key feature is the avoidance of random oracles in the security proof, instead defining explicit standard model requirements for the underlying hash functions.

title: Lean Consensus: 2026 Plan
quote: Lean Consensus (formerly Beam Chain) represents a modernized Ethereum Consensus Layer redesign incorporating MEV, zero-knowledge technology, and advanced consensus mechanisms into a single hard fork. XMSS replaces BLS signatures with hash-based, quantum-resistant signatures, using Poseidon2 for circuit efficiency: a many-time signature structure where a Merkle tree commits to a sequence of one-time public keys. LeanVM is a minimal zkVM purpose-built for signature aggregation, operating on the KoalaBear prime field (p = 2^31 - 2^24 + 1) with POSEIDON_16/24, DOT_PRODUCT and MULTILINEAR_EVAL precompiles. Decoupled three-layer consensus: ChFast (Goldfish / GHOST-Eph) for block production, ChMaj (RLMD) for the majority-filtered justified chain, ChFin (BFT) for economic finality. 2026 targets: aggregate 1,000 XMSS signatures per second; 2-to-1 recursive proof in ~200ms; propagate a 256KB SNARK in under one second; 5+ client implementations; 10,000 validators in a long-running devnet of more than one month; monthly devnet launches.

title: The Extremely Lean Chain
quote: Pushing responsibility to stakers to manage and occasionally ZK-prove their state. Phase 1A replaces the 48-byte pubkey with a 5-byte deposit tree index; Phase 1B retains only 6 bytes per validator on-chain. At the end of each day, a validator is required to generate a STARK that walks through the chain since the previous day. At 1M validators that is more than 100 STARKs per slot, requiring aggregation. This removes the burdens of end-of-epoch processing and may allow consensus to scale to millions of validators if needed. Open problems include validator inactivity eviction, proof inclusion incentives (rational proposers might censor balance updates), social slashing coordination which would have to be more explicitly wargamed, and the risk that privacy features obfuscate centralization.

title: Poseidon Cryptanalysis Initiative
quote: Poseidon and Poseidon2 are hash functions designed for the use in verifiable computation protocols, optimized for the smallest circuit size over prime fields. The initiative aims to determine whether Poseidon is secure for high-value applications and foundations of Ethereum. 2026 bounty program $150,000; 2025 bounty program $130,000; collision prize $992,000 until Jan 1 2029; attack reward program 2026 $90,000. CICO problem solutions were verified in April, May and July 2026 across different round configurations; the Zero-test problem has been broken up to RF=6, RP=12 (claimed July 27, 2026).

title: Lean Execution: a holistic approach to secure, efficient, adaptive, and resourceful execution throughput to scale the world-computer
quote: How can we ensure that the Ethereum protocol remains provably secure ... sufficiently high in throughput; maximally simple; and optimally decentralized? Rather than modifying the EVM itself, Lean Execution leverages SNARKs to verify arbitrary computation in constant time, decoupling verification costs from execution costs. The architecture progresses from single-threaded execution toward parallel execution committees organized via recursive SNARK aggregation (execution trees).

title: Justin Drake proposes 'Beam Chain,' an Ethereum consensus layer redesign
leanEthereum/leanVM — Minimal zkVM for Ethereum (formerly leanMultisig)
quote: leanVM is a minimal hash-based zero-knowledge virtual machine. Proof system combines WHIR (multilinear variant), SuperSpartan for AIR constraints, and Logup bus-based lookups. XMSS aggregation throughput 1,426-1,550 signatures/second at WHIR rate 1/2; proof sizes 122-327 KiB depending on configuration; recursive aggregation combines previously-aggregated batches of 700 XMSS each. Field is the KoalaBear prime with degree-5 extension; hash digests are 4 field elements (~124 bits); provable security ~124 bits (Johnson bound). NIST Level 1 security (128/64 bits classical/quantum) remains in progress and requires either larger hash digests (5 elements) or alternative primes (Goldilocks branch under development). Conservative security analysis (ROM/QROM) in progress.

title: pq-devnet-1 specification (leanEthereum/pm)
quote: Implement leanSig post-quantum signature signing & verification in lean consensus clients, with naive signature aggregation and baseline performance metrics. 5 validators, one per client instance, 4-second slot durations. PQ signature parameters: Hash chains: 64, Chain length: 8, Max lifetime: 2^32, Activation time: 2^18. Participating clients: Ream, Zeam, Qlean, Lantern, Grandine. Naive aggregation by concatenating individual signatures. Validator set is pre-determined and fixed at genesis.

title: Beginnings of a Post-Quantum Ethereum
quote: Devnet 0 completed at the Cambridge PQ Interop, October 4-6 2025, with Ream (Rust), Zeam (Zig) and Quadrivium (C++) proving P2P cross client interoperability and messaging semantics. Devnet 1 was planned as the first devnet to run one of Lean's core technologies end to end: post quantum signatures. Hash-based signatures often have larger signatures and demand careful record keeping to prevent one-time key reuse, affecting gossip bandwidth, block size planning, and storage. Key lifecycle and tooling become central. If Lean adopts stateful hash based schemes like XMSS or LMS validators will need reliable key rotation tracking and backup workflows. Without cheap pairing based aggregation new merkle or hash multisig approaches or heavier per validator costs may alter reward and slash models.

title: Ethereum Signature Schemes Explained: ECDSA, BLS, XMSS, and Post-Quantum leanSig with Rust Code Examples
quote: BLS signature size: 48 bytes. XMSS/hash-based signature size: ~2,500 bytes; public key 8 elements. leanSig: ~3kB signature, 8-element public key, signing and verification target < 0.5ms, key lifetime 8 years. leanMultisig aggregate proof size ~100 KB (constant size!). Use a SNARK (STARK) to prove that N individual XMSS signatures are valid. The 'aggregate signature' is the SNARK proof. Aggregator uses a SNARK prover to prove all N signatures are valid, aggregating hundreds of XMSS signatures per second on consumer hardware.

title: Post-quantum cryptography on Ethereum
quote: This is not an imminent threat. But cryptographic transitions take years, and Ethereum's security model is designed to last centuries. Google's 2026 research suggests breaking Ethereum's current cryptography could require roughly 1,200 logical qubits, potentially arriving sometime around the end of this decade at the earliest. Four vulnerable areas: BLS signatures in the consensus layer, KZG commitments for data availability, ECDSA on secp256k1 for accounts, and pairing-based SNARKs at the application layer. Mitigations: leanXMSS plus leanVM for BLS; STARK or lattice-based commitments for KZG; account abstraction (EIP-8141) so individual accounts could switch to a post-quantum signature scheme without waiting for the entire protocol to change. Target completion of core post-quantum infrastructure ~2029 via milestones I, J, L, M with planned hard forks.

title: Quantum computing and blockchains: Matching urgency to actual threats
quote: A cryptographically relevant quantum computer arriving in the 2020s is highly unlikely, and a 5-10 year window is unsupported by publicly known progress. Blockchains should still follow the web's deliberate approach to signature migration. Signatures have no harvest-now-decrypt-later vulnerability, warranting deliberate rather than immediate migration. Implementation vulnerabilities will be a far bigger security risk than a cryptographically relevant quantum computer for years to come.

title: Ethereum developers embrace Vitalik Buterin's long-term vision but urge quicker execution
quote: Eli Ben-Sasson (StarkWare co-founder): '3-4 years' as the timeline is way too long. Especially for quantum readiness. Dankrad Feist (former Ethereum Foundation researcher): 'But 3-4 years is very slow. I think we should be ambitious and get it done in ~1 year.' Ben-Sasson also questioned specific technical proposals: 'New kinds of state: what does that mean? Who is affected by it?'

title: Ethereum outlines roadmap for 'Lean Ethereum' upgrades targeting 10,000 TPS and quantum safety
quote: The roadmap was formalized through what the Ethereum Foundation calls a 'strawmap,' a draft strategic framework showcased at an internal workshop in January 2026. Seven distinct upgrades are planned through 2029, organized around three priorities: scaling, improved user experience, and Layer 1 hardening against quantum threats. L1 mainnet target approximately 10,000 TPS; L2 approximately 1 million TPS; current Ethereum 15-30 TPS. Glamsterdam is scheduled for the latter half of 2026 as the first concrete implementation step. Roadmaps are not releases. Ethereum has a long history of ambitious timelines that slip, sometimes by years.

title: Lean Ethereum · Pattern · EthSystems
quote: Lean Ethereum is a long-range redesign of the Ethereum consensus layer, targeting a single major fork, with four primary objectives: post-quantum signatures, zkVM-based proof compression, reduced hardware/stake requirements for validators, and networking upgrades. The target is a consensus protocol that is stable for decades, resilient against quantum adversaries, and verifiable on minimal devices. Pillars include hash-based multisignatures (XMSS/Winternitz family), minimal zkVMs, Gossipsub v2 and rateless set reconciliation, lower solo-staking thresholds, and formal verification (Lean 4) of signature aggregation and consensus logic. Trade-offs: multi-year research horizon with heavy dependence on open research questions; single bundled fork means a failure in one component delays the entire upgrade; consensus-only scope; heavy coordination overhead across many teams. Last reviewed 2026-06-18.

title: blockblaz/zeam — Ethereum Lean client in Zig (wip)
quote: Zeam is a production-grade implementation (work-in-progress) of the Beam Chain, a ZK-based Ethereum Consensus Protocol unveiled at Devcon 7 Bangkok (November 2024). Beam Chain is designed to upgrade the current Beacon Chain by massively scaling and decentralizing Ethereum consensus through provable, ZK-VM-backed state transitions.

title: Introducing ethlambda: A Lean Consensus Client for Ethereum's Next Era
quote: ethlambda is a Lean Consensus client. The client integrates with lean-quickstart, so spinning up a local devnet with ethlambda alongside Zeam and Ream is a single command.

title: Goldfish: No More Attacks on Ethereum?!
venue: arXiv / Financial Cryptography and Data Security (FC 2024)
quote: LMD GHOST, a critical component of proof-of-stake Ethereum, is brittle in its current form, as evidenced by recent attacks and patching attempts. We propose Goldfish, a new protocol that is secure in the sleepy model, is reorg resilient so that honestly produced blocks are guaranteed inclusion in the ledger, and supports fast confirmation with expected confirmation latency independent of the desired security level. Crucially, Goldfish is structurally similar to LMD GHOST, providing a credible path to adoption in Ethereum.

title: Minimmit: Fast Finality with Even Faster Blocks
quote: There has been significant recent interest in State-Machine-Replication (SMR) protocols that achieve 2-round finality under the assumption that 5f+1 <= n, where n is the number of processors and f bounds the number of processors that may exhibit Byzantine faults. Core contribution: view progression and transaction finality can operate on different quorum thresholds without compromising safety or liveness. Testing on 50 globally distributed processors showed a 23.1% reduction in view latency and a 10.7% reduction in transaction latency compared to the state-of-the-art. Neither Ethereum nor lean consensus is referenced.

title: Lean Ethereum: the biggest overhaul of Ethereum since The Merge
quote: The ambition is no longer to improve the protocol at the margins, but to progressively rebuild its core building blocks. Lean Data replaces KZG commitments with quantum-resistant hash-based mechanisms; a sufficiently powerful quantum computer could recover the secret hidden behind the KZG trusted setup, then forge false proofs — Google Quantum AI (March 2026) estimated roughly 1,500 logical qubits. Targets: finality ~15 min to ~8 sec, slots 12s to 4s, gas limit 60M to ~200M, L1 10,000 TPS, L2 1 GB/sec (~10M TPS), fault tolerance threshold ~33% to 17%. Fork sequence: Glamsterdam (H2 2026, EIP-7732 and EIP-7928), Hegota (FOCIL), then I* as the first fully Lean-oriented upgrade and L* as the bundled Lean Consensus deployment concentrating implementation risk. The Strawmap structures seven forks through 2029. Criticisms: dependencies span zkVMs, peer-to-peer protocols and multi-client implementations, so delays cascade; the Ethereum Foundation 2026 budget was cut about 40% with 54 positions eliminated; Dankrad Feist argued the 3-4 year horizon is unnecessary. Poseidon2 was initially considered but recent cryptanalyses prompted a shift toward avoiding dependence on a single hash function.

title: Ethereum is about to replace itself: Inside the Lean Rebuild
quote: Glamsterdam brings a large gas increase; Hegota, expected later in 2026, is likely the final upgrade of the pre-Lean age. Five north stars: fast finality on layer 1, gigagas-level throughput on layer 1, teragas-scale data availability for layer 2, post-quantum security, and native protocol-level privacy. Verification by proof becomes, in Buterin's words, an enshrined first-class core component. RISC-V and leanISA are contenders, with the EVM preserved as a compatibility layer. Quantum safety has shifted up a lot in priority, with a target of full post-quantum coverage by 2029. Three to four years, on this record, reads to many as the optimistic bound of a five-to-eight-year reality.

title: ethlambda: devnet 5 and beyond
quote: Published 16 Jun 2026. Instead of gossiping one single-message aggregate per attestation, we now gossip a single block proof covering all attestations. A block carrying max attestations drops from several MBs to around 200KB. Ethlambda and other clients have implemented devnet 5, and teams are running interop devnets to find issues. For devnet 6 the main candidate is a mix of three algorithms: Goldfish, RLMD-GHOST, and a trailing finality gadget. Goldfish is an algorithm similar to LMD-GHOST, with a more rigorous approach to synchronization; it considers only votes from the current slot. RLMD-GHOST counts votes from the last N slots, with N a protocol parameter.

title: Fork Choice in leanConsensus: How ethlambda Implements LMD-GHOST
quote: Published 17 Mar 2026. leanConsensus implements LMD-GHOST for fork choice and 3SF-mini for finality as its two core consensus components. The same LMD-GHOST algorithm computes a conservative safe target using a supermajority threshold of ceil(2V/3), which feeds into 3SF-mini for finalization decisions. Slot structure: 4-second slots divided into 5 intervals of 800ms each — interval 0 block proposal and fork choice, interval 1 attestation creation, interval 3 safe-target recalculation, interval 4 attestations promoted to active and head updated. Once a checkpoint is finalized, all blocks at or before it can be discarded from the fork choice working set entirely.

title: Claiming bounties on small scale Poseidon and Poseidon2 instances using resultant-based algebraic attacks
quote: In november 2024, the Ethereum foundation (EF) issued a bounty program with challenges on Poseidon and Poseidon2. The goal of these challenges is to find CICO solutions on different round-reduced instances of Poseidon and Poseidon2, defined on different prime fields. The researchers solved three instances of Poseidon2-31m and Poseidon2-31k using a new resultant-based approach, and two instances of Poseidon-256 relying on already-known univariate root finding.

title: Ethereum Glamsterdam Upgrade Explained: ePBS, BAL, and the 200M Gas Limit Path
quote: Published 01 Jul 2026. Glamsterdam — combining the Amsterdam execution layer and Gloas consensus layer upgrades — is the network's most ambitious protocol overhaul since the Merge. Headline EIPs: EIP-7732 (ePBS), EIP-7928 (Block-Level Access Lists), EIP-8037, EIP-8038, EIP-7954, EIP-7997, EIP-7708, EIP-2780, EIP-8159. Gas limit target 200 million; expected mainnet September 16 2026 (tentative), Sepolia activation August 3 2026 (tentative). ePBS extends the execution payload propagation window from roughly 2 seconds to about 9 seconds. State growth at a 200 million gas limit would exceed 380 GiB per year. No post-quantum or lean-consensus items are included.

title: Upgrading Ethereum — 2.9.2 Curve BLS12-381
quote: the public key (48 bytes) and signature (96 bytes). G1 points are reduced from 96 bytes (2 x 381 bits-rounded-to-bytes) to 48 bytes, and G2 points are reduced from 192 bytes to 96 bytes. In Ethereum 2.0 we use G1 for public keys: for one thing, aggregation of public keys happens much more often than aggregation of signatures; for another, public keys of validators need to be stored in state, so keeping the representation small is important.

title: Ethereum Researcher Justin Drake Proposes Beam Chain Redesign, but Not All OGs Are Onboard
quote: Justin Drake proposed Beam Chain, a redesign of Ethereum's consensus layer, at Ethereum's Devcon conference in Bangkok, on a five-year roadmap with completion by 2029-2030, featuring improved transaction finality time, integration of zero-knowledge technology, 4-second blocks, and quantum resistance. Ethereum core developer Peter Szilagyi warned: 'we should be [wary] of introducing too many changes at once that impact everything across the board.' Ethereum builder Martin Koppelmann criticized the proposal as insufficiently ambitious: 'The big new feature is... a big refactoring. Sorry @DrakeFJustin, but [in my opinion] Ethereum needs to be more ambitious.' EigenLayer principal engineer Bowen Li on the timeline: 'My eyes HURT when seeing anything Ethereum present[s] takes 5 [years] to ship.' Delphi Digital founding partner Jose Maria Macedo called it disappointing, stating the proposal wouldn't enhance competitiveness or create compelling narrative momentum.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography and Quantum-Safe Security: A Comprehensive Survey
quote: SPHINCS+ (SLH-DSA) produces signatures of 7,856 bytes at NIST Security Level 1, with signing times near 131 ms; SLH-DSA-256s produces signatures of 29,792 bytes. Its security relies solely on the preimage and collision resistance of cryptographic hash functions, providing the most conservative class of post-quantum primitives. ML-DSA-44 (CRYSTALS-Dilithium) produces 2,420 byte signatures; ML-DSA-87 generates 4,595 byte signatures; security rests on the module short integer solution and module learning with errors problems. Falcon-512 signatures measure only 666 bytes at Level 1 and Falcon-1024 produces 1,280 byte signatures, but reliance on the NTRU assumption - less extensively analyzed than MLWE - leaves open long-term theoretical questions.
